items.bold: WASHINGTON POST (May 25, 7:42AM EDT): US-Iran FRAMEWORK confirmed — 60-day ceasefire extension + Hormuz DE-MINED + REOPENED while final deal negotiated.
items.text: Washington Post (9 hours ago) confirmed by a senior administration official: The United States and Iran have developed a "framework" that extends their ceasefire 60 days as the two sides reach a "final deal" to end the war in Iran, while in the meantime, the Strait of Hormuz would be de-mined and reopened. This is the single most important confirmed diplomatic development of the 88-day war. The framework has three components: (1) 60-day ceasefire extension — buys time for final deal negotiations, (2) Hormuz de-mining — critical for safe VLCC transit to resume, (3) Hormuz reopened — commercial traffic returns before nuclear issue resolved. The strategic significance: Hormuz reopening is DECOUPLED from nuclear final deal. India does not need to wait for the nuclear question to be resolved before LPG and fertiliser carriers can transit Hormuz again. Brent falls on Hormuz reopening regardless of nuclear outcome. CENTCOM Admiral Cooper previously confirmed 90% of mines destroyed — de-mining the remaining 10% could take weeks to months.

items.text: CNN live (44 minutes ago) confirmed: oil prices dropped sharply on Monday after US officials signaled that the United States and Iran had edged closer to a peace deal that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Both countries have since downplayed chances of a successful deal being signed soon. Plenty of uncertainty remains over the exact status of the negotiations and the specific terms. Brent crude fell roughly 6% to about $97 a barrel — down from $104 at market close on Friday — but still much higher than the $74 a barrel price before the war. WTI also fell by 6% to about $90. The downplaying by both sides after the WaPo framework report suggests: (1) the framework is real but not yet signed, (2) both Iran and the US want to manage expectations, (3) specific terms — particularly on nuclear and Hormuz tolls — are still being finalised. Markets correctly read this: Brent fell 6% (framework positive) but not to $80 (deal signed would cause).

items.text: The WaPo framework confirmation has extraordinary strategic significance for India specifically: The framework decouples Hormuz reopening from the nuclear final deal. Under the framework: (1) Hormuz is de-mined and reopened during the 60-day extension, (2) nuclear negotiations continue separately during the same period, (3) commercial traffic resumes before nuclear issue is resolved. This means: India's LPG imports (60% via Hormuz), kharif fertiliser (35% of urea via Gulf), and crude imports can all resume BEFORE the nuclear question between Trump/Netanyahu and Iran is settled. CENTCOM Admiral Cooper confirmed 90% of mines destroyed — de-mining the remaining 10% likely takes 2-6 weeks. Brent will fall to $80-85 when de-mining is confirmed complete and Hormuz is open to VLCC traffic. For India: the framework, even without a final nuclear deal, is worth an estimated Rs 80,000-100,000 Cr annual import bill saving compared to the $104/barrel pre-framework level.

assessment.body:
Tuesday 9:45 AM IST. Day 88. The framework is real. The signing is not.

THE WASHINGTON POST FRAMEWORK
Confirmed by a senior administration official, May 25, 7:42 AM EDT:
"The United States and Iran have developed a framework that extends their ceasefire 60 days as the two sides reach a final deal to end the war in Iran, while in the meantime, the Strait of Hormuz would be de-mined and reopened."
Three components:
→ 60-day ceasefire extension
→ Hormuz de-mined
→ Hormuz reopened
All three happen WHILE nuclear final deal is still being negotiated.

THE DOWNPLAYING
CNN (44 minutes ago): both countries downplayed chances of deal being signed soon.
The framework is real. The signed agreement is not yet.
Specific gaps remain: nuclear dismantlement vs retention, Hormuz without tolls vs PGSA system.
But: framework existence means the architecture is agreed. What remains is signing.

MONDAY'S HISTORIC CLOSE
Sensex: +1,073.61 pts (+1.42%) to 76,488.96
Nifty: +312.40 pts (+1.32%) to 24,031.70
ABOVE 24,000 — first time since the war began on February 28.
15 of 16 sectoral indices closed green.
Nifty Bank +2%. Rupee strengthened sharply.
Emkay Nifty 29,000 March 2027: now on structural trajectory.

THE FRAMEWORK's STRATEGIC SIGNIFICANCE FOR INDIA
Hormuz is DECOUPLED from nuclear resolution.
Under the framework: India's LPG, fertiliser, and crude imports resume BEFORE the nuclear question between Trump/Netanyahu and Iran is settled.
De-mining: CENTCOM Cooper confirmed 90% of mines destroyed.
Remaining 10%: 2-6 weeks.
Brent trajectory: $97 now → $80-85 when de-mining complete.
India annual import bill saving: Rs 1.2 lakh crore at $82 vs $104.

INDIA'S TUESDAY
Cautious open after +1,073 Monday.
Both sides downplaying = profit-taking at 24,000.
Nifty 24,000 support: if it holds → structural bull. If it breaks → retest 23,800.
PGSA applications: submit today — de-mining still requires coordination.
Kharif fertiliser: order today for delivery post-de-mining.
Haji Ali protest: file today.

VERDICT: Day 88 is the morning after the most important diplomatic confirmation of the 88-day war. The Washington Post's framework report, confirmed by a senior administration official, decouples Hormuz reopening from the nuclear final deal. India's energy emergency can end — in 2-6 weeks — even while Trump and Netanyahu's nuclear condition remains unresolved with Iran. The Nifty has crossed 24,000. Brent has fallen below $100. The framework is the map. The question is who signs it, and when.
